questions: Does y=0.07 lower oval max_error below 0.0598 and keep oval progress at or above 0.87? If progress falls, the row is too far ahead for the straights.
Do s-bend and slalom max_error move below 0.061? If they stay at 0.061 or above, bend exits are not sensing-limited and geometry should stop changing.
Does steering_oscillation on the oval rise above 0.34? If it does, the controller needs more damping, not more geometry.
Does line_loss_events stay at or below 1.0 per run on every track?

intent: Test a single change from the best geometry: move the five 16 mm sensors from y=0.06 to y=0.07 (x=±0.04, ±0.02, 0), keeping wheel_track 0.09 m, body 0.22 m by 0.12 m, mass 0.5 kg and wheel radius 0.03 m. Goal: lower oval max_error below 0.06 further and move s-bend and slalom max_error below the off-track limit, while keeping oval progress at or above 0.85.
learning: Iteration 7 confirmed that the iteration 3 geometry reproduces at 203.20 with oval progress 0.87, so the platform is stable. Narrowing the track (iteration 6) and widening the outer pair (iteration 4) both lowered progress, and 12 mm footprints (iteration 5) did too. Forward sensing is the only geometry lever that has improved the oval. This iteration tests whether a further forward step to y=0.07 continues that gain. If it does not, the next geometry change is unlikely to help, and remaining work belongs to the controller.
rationale: The restored iteration 7 run reproduced the iteration 3 best exactly (score 203.20). Oval progress was 0.87, which meets the Integrator's 0.85 condition. S-bend and slalom max_error stayed at 0.0615 and 0.0611, still at or above 0.061, so the condition for the next geometry step is met. The only geometry change that has moved the oval is forward sensing. Moving the row from y=0.04 to y=0.06 cut oval max_error from 0.0617 to 0.0598 and raised progress from 0.53 to 0.87. Outer spacing (x=±0.05), footprint size (12 mm) and track width (0.085 m) all cost progress without moving the bend exits. The bend exits have stayed at 0.061 to 0.064 across every geometry since iteration 2, so the next single test is whether even earlier sensing lowers them. I therefore move the sensor row to y=0.07, keeping x=±0.04 at 16 mm, and hold every other geometry value at the iteration 7 best. Expected result: oval max_error slightly below 0.06 and oval progress at or above 0.87, with some risk that steering_oscillation rises above 0.34 because the loop gains effectively increase. If the bend exits do not move, geometry should stop changing and the Integrator should carry the rest on the controller side.
